title: gpu-infra-cost-modeling-lab-notebook-and-synthetic-workload-catalog
author: Maya Rodriguez
content:
Summary:
This lab notebook documents the synthetic workload catalog and the reproducible methodology our infrastructure team uses to model GPU fleet cost and capacity under production-like load. It combines workload templates, CI harness steps, IaC knobs, and runbook guidance so engineers can (1) estimate unit economics, (2) validate autoscaler behavior, and (3) produce artifacts for SRE/finance reviews.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a repeatable, shareable process for converting observed or hypothesized request patterns into a cost + SLO projection tied to concrete IaC variables and CI artifacts.
- Scope: Redwood Inference hosted and dedicated modes; synthetic workloads target text-generation (autoregressive), chat multi-turn, embedding-only, and KV-replay warmup. Does NOT cover private on-prem hardware procurement process.

Owners and contacts:
- Primary owner: Maya Rodriguez (infra-cost@redwood.ai)
- Secondary: Arjun Patel (gpu-fleet@redwood.ai)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major runtime kernel/quantization change.

When to use this notebook:
1. Prior to committing a new reserved GPU capacity contract (predict 6/12 month unit costs).
2. When validating an alternate quantization/kernel rollout (measure token cost delta).
3. To simulate multi-account burst scenarios and verify fair-share throttling.

Definitions and abbreviations:
- TPU: not used here; we target NVIDIA A100/A800/GPU types in fleet catalog.
- Unit token: billing unit used in hosted API; modeled as average token length per request.
- KV-warmup: warm prefix state loaded into runtime KV cache for faster generation.

Synthetic workload catalog (canonical):
Note: each workload entry is a named template that maps to a CI job and a Terraform variable set. Use these names in automation.

| id | name | dominant pattern | seq_len_percentile | concurrency | key_i/o | purpose | example params |
|----|------|------------------|--------------------|-------------|---------|---------|----------------|
| W1 | regen-1k-short | autoregressive short responses (search assistant) | p50=16 p95=64 | 50 rps | none | baseline latency/cost | prompt=16 tokens, response=32 tokens |
| W2 | convo-10-turn | multi-turn chat with KV warmup | p50=32 p95=256 | 20 sessions | kv=warmup(3 turns) | validate KV cache hit rate | session_length=10, avg_turn=48 |
| W3 | embeddings-batch-4 | batched embedding calls | fixed=512 dims | batch_size=4 | 200 qps | cost-per-embed analysis | batch_size=4, payload=512d |
| W4 | long-context-eval | long-context generation (LLM evals) | p50=512 p95=2048 | 5 rps | partial-kv | stress memory, kernel selection | prompt=1024, response=512 |
| W5 | quantized-fractional | fractional GPU multiplexing with 4-way packing | p50=32 p95=128 | 120 tenants | none | multiplexing efficiency | pack=4, memory_limit=70% |
| W6 | preemptive-spot-burst | spot-eviction and burst fallback | variable | simulated preemptions | warmpool=true | ensure graceful fallback | spot_drop_rate=0.01 |

For each workload we track the following measurement vector (CI artifact outputs):
- mean_latency_ms, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms
- tokens_generated, tokens_per_sec
- GPU_util_pct, GPU_mem_used_mb, host_cpu_pct
- KV_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_histogram
- infra_cost_usd_hour, per_token_cost_usd (derived)

Benchmark methodology (reproducible steps):
1) Choose workload template (W1..W6) and target region/account.
2) Create a feature branch in infra-lab repo: refs/heads/lab/<workload>-<date>.
3) Update terraform variables under labs/overrides/<workload>.tfvars with: desired_node_type, reserved_count, warm_pool_size, preempt_strategy.
4) Trigger CI job lab/ci-run-benchmark that performs:
   a) IaC apply (using a gated sandbox account with cost limits).
   b) Deploy runtime image tagged lab-<sha>.
   c) Run workload generator (see workload generator CLI snippet below) for 30–120 minutes.
   d) Collect telemetry via telemetry-collector service and push artifacts to S3: metrics.json, traces.pb, gpu-proc-stats.csv.
5) Post-process artifacts with cost-model script (Python): outputs per-token cost and projected monthly spend for 1M/10M/100M tokens.

Workload generator CLI example:

workload-runner --template W2 --region us-west-2 --concurrency 20 --duration 3600 --output s3://redwood-lab-artifacts/<run-id>/

Cost projection knobs and Terraform mapping:
- reserved_gpu_count -> terraform var: reserved_count (integer)
- reserved_gpu_type -> node_type (e.g., g5, a100-sxm)
- warm_pool_size -> warm_pool_count (integer)
- kv_eviction_policy -> module.runtime.kv_policy (string)
- quant_profile -> module.runtime.quant_profile (enum: int8,int4,fp16)
- burst_credit_pool -> module.scheduler.burst_credits (float)
Example tfvars snippet (apply in labs sandbox):

# labs/overrides/W5.tfvars
reserved_count = 8
node_type = "a100-sxm-80gb"
warm_pool_count = 2
quant_profile = "int8"

CI/CD integration and templates:
- Pipeline: buildkite/labs-bench -> steps: apply-iac (manual), deploy-runtime, run-benchmark, postprocess, notify.
- Artifact naming convention: <workload>-<region>-<sha>-<timestamp>.tar.gz
- Gate: apply-iac requires approval from infra-cost owner if predicted hourly cost > $50/hr.

Interpreting outputs and acceptance criteria:
- Cost acceptance: per_token_cost_usd must not exceed baseline by more than +12% unless justified (kernel/quantization benefit elsewhere).
- Latency SLO: p95_generation_latency <= SLO for the tenant class (default: 350ms for short-gen workloads).
- Warmup effectiveness: KV_cache_hit_rate >= 0.85 after 10 minutes of session simulation.
- Multiplexing efficiency: for pack=4, GPU_util_pct should be >= 72% and memory headroom >= 12%.

Runbook: common failures and remediation:
- Symptom: GPU util low but tokens/sec low.
  - Cause: small batch sizes or request serialization in client harness.
  - Action: increase synthetic concurrency or enable async batching in workload-runner.
- Symptom: KV cache miss rate high on W2.
  - Cause: incorrect warm_pool_size or mismatch in session key derivation between generator and runtime.
  - Action: verify warm_pool_count in tfvars and run generator with --kv-keys-file matching runtime seed.
- Symptom: Ci job aborted due to cost cap.
  - Action: escalate to infra-cost owner; rerun with smaller node_count or in a lower-cost region.

Network and multi-account considerations:
- Use test accounts prefixed labs-<team>-<env> and ensure cross-account peering is disabled unless explicitly required.
- Egress budgeting: enable egress-metering in tfvars: egress_metering = true so cost-model includes NAT/transfer fees.
- For cross-account burst simulations, use the burst-simulator module (labs/modules/burst-sim) with controlled synthetic spikes and a configurable window.

IaC module checklist (for lab experiments):
- modules/runtime: expose quant_profile, kv_policy, cpu_request, memory_request, warm_pool_count.
- modules/scheduler: expose burst_credits, preempt_policy, pack_factor.
- modules/network: lab-mode toggles to disable external peers and force local egress route.
- modules/observability: enable telemetry sidecar with shippers to S3-for-labs and low-retention Prometheus remote_write.

Artifacts and storage conventions:
- Raw metrics: s3://redwood-lab-artifacts/raw/<run-id>/metrics.json
- Processed report: s3://redwood-lab-artifacts/reports/<workload>-<date>.html
- Cost model outputs: s3://redwood-lab-artifacts/cost-model/<run-id>/cost.csv

Template analysis report (fields we produce):
- run_id, workload, region, node_type, reserved_count, mean_latency_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, gpu_util_pct, per_token_cost_usd, projected_monthly_usd_10M_tokens

Decision guidance and handoff:
- Include the generated report as part of PR when requesting purchase of reserved capacity. Finance will accept reports with clear assumptions: 24/7 utilization, expected burst delta, and forecasted growth rate.

Change log (selected):
- 2024-05-12: initial notebook and W1-W4 templates created (Maya Rodriguez).
- 2024-09-03: added quantized-fractional workload and tfvars template (Arjun Patel).
- 2025-02-17: CI gating change: require manual approval if estimated hourly cost > $50/hr (Simone Lefevre).

Appendix: quick troubleshooting snippets
- Generate run id and start workload:
  RUN_ID=$(date +%s)-${BUILDKITE_COMMIT}
  workload-runner --template W1 --concurrency 50 --duration 3600 --run-id ${RUN_ID} --output s3://redwood-lab-artifacts/raw/${RUN_ID}/

- Post-process locally (example):
  python infra-lab/tools/cost_model.py --input s3://redwood-lab-artifacts/raw/${RUN_ID}/metrics.json --out cost.csv --assume-hours-per-day 24

Notes and caveats:
- Synthetic workloads approximate production but cannot capture external client-side batching or realtime user-side rate-limiting patterns. Always pair synthetic runs with short real-traffic shadow-tests.
- Lab sandbox quotas are limited; schedule long runs off-peak and coordinate with gpu-fleet oncall.

Related resources:
- Repo: git@github.com:redwood-infra/infra-lab.git (labs/ directory)
- Runbook: eng-infra/runbooks/preflight-gpu-deployment-validation-and-rollback-playbook.json

Feedback and improvements:
- Add new workload templates when we onboard a new model family (seq2seq, mixture-of-experts).
- Improve postprocess to include uncertainty bands for cloud price volatility.

End of notebook.
